full_judgment:
Syed J. R. Mudassir Husain, C J: This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 9.11.2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2839 of 2004 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure discharging the Rule arising out of an Order dated 14.02.2004 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Metro Criminal Revision Case 173 of 2003 in dismissing the Criminal Revision thereby affirming the order dated 23,03.2003 passed by Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in C. R. Case No. 2282 of 2002 in dropping the proceedings under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. The complainant petitioner made a petition of complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka under section 107/117C of the Code of Criminal Procedure alleging therein that he is peace loving man, on the contrary the opposite parties are notorious persons and they have a profession to occupy others land. The complainant got some lands by inheritance. The respondents threatened the complainant for going away leaving the property otherwise they would title false case and would dispossess the complainant from the case land. On 29.8.2001, the respondents led by respondent No. 1 at about 5 P.M. when the petitioner, came out of his house to market, abused him and threatened for beating. The learned Magistrate on 7.9.2002, on perusal of the petition of complaint, issued show cause notice upon the accused opposite parties. Thereafter, the case was transferred to the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka who on 28. 11. 2002 received the case records and fixed 12. 12. 2002 for hearing. But the learned Magistrate could not hear the matter on 12.12.2002, 21.1.2003, 6.2.2002 and 16.3.2003 and ultimately it was taken up for hearing on 23.3.2003 when the learned Magistrate was of the opinion that the complaint petition does not call for any investigation and thus dropped the proceeding. Against the said order, the complainant moved the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge in Criminal Revision No.173 of 2003 on 23.3.2003. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his order dated 14.2.2004 dismissed the revision and upheld the order of the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. 

 4. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, contended that the Magistrate in dealing with the proceeding under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure ought to have passed judgment/order upon evidence relevant to the case. But in the instant case without taking any evidence and without hearing the parties and without considering the complainant materials as a whole, illegally dropped the proceedings under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the learned Session Judge as well as the High Court Division did not consider this aspect of the case the and thus committed error. 

 5. We have considered the submission. On perusal of the judgment of the High Court Division, we find that the learned Judges of the High Court Division meticulously considered the case of both the parties and it appears that the High Court Division upon perusal of the petition of complainant found that it does not disclose any material attracting action under Section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The High Court Division in our view has meticulously considered the case of the parties in their perspective and found that the learned Magistrate was perfectly within his jurisdiction to drop the proceedings. 

 6. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we are fully in agreement with the findings and decisions arrived at by the High Court Division. In such view of the matter, this petition merits no consideration and accordingly it is dismissed.
